source: tools/simulation/meta.py, check.py, exit_lab.py, window_select.py, marks.py, oracle.py, review.py at commit b63b9015
notes: The meta stage is compared end to end. The window, marks, oracle, review, check, and exit cases compare the reductions the checked-in mini bundle can exercise; each case names its omission. The historical SIM-01..SIM-10 runs cannot be replayed because their external data root is not in the repository, and the existing Rust stages are a redesign rather than a literal Python port.

cases.name: sim-03-exit-lab
cases.notes: SIM-03 exit reduction on the mini bundle. Fixed, time, and partial are compared in R; the Python EMA and swing trails are not compared because the Rust lab computes its own EMA and has no swing policy. Cost is zero so the R conversion is exact.

cases.name: window-full-span
cases.notes: Degenerate full-span window: with the 400-bar mini bundle, a 400-bar window, and a candidate at bar 60, the Python selector and the Rust equal-span selector both return [0, 400). This is the only window shape where the two selectors are comparable without the Python event-centred candidate logic.

cases.name: marks-balanced-set
cases.notes: The mark schema accepts the balanced oracle set on a 61-bar window. The Python validator also derives marked_time_utc; the Rust schema leaves the timestamp to the server boundary, so only acceptance and the bar identities are compared.

cases.name: marks-outside-window
cases.notes: A mark outside the chart is refused by both validators. The Python validator keys on the chart bar list; the Rust validator keys on the window range.

cases.name: oracle-single-candidate
cases.notes: One candidate at bar 60. The forward return is the Python short path's long-oriented close-to-close result from the entry close to its rule exit at bar 70. With one candidate the Rust oracle marks the short good and emits no bad mark, matching the Python entry mark.

cases.name: review-counts
cases.notes: The review count primitive on the balanced oracle set. The Python count_by_quality and the Rust Counts use the same quality and side buckets; the agreement and disagreement lists are not part of this comparison.
